item.title: after work bike ride on the ATT — Tue Aug 4, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Triangle Hiking and Outdoors Group We'll be starting near Southpoint and final starting point will be sent out Monday evening.
Make sure that your bike is in good working order - tires hold air and are up to pressure, brakes and shifters work and your chain has been oiled.
We'll be riding 2 1/4 hours and about 25 miles. The ride is fairly flat and shaded and our pace will be moderate (about 12 mph average). I recommend a hard tail or hybrid bike, but if you really want to bring a road bike it's ok, though you'll likely be a bit bored. Unicycles....?
I'll be eating after the ride at a restaurant. You're welcome to join me if you like.
Helmets are required and by signing up you agree to THOG liability waiver statement.
Please Note!! Any cancellation less than 30 hours before the beginning of the event will be considered a "no show"

item.description:

It includes total cholesterol, blood pressure, blood glucose, BMI, waist circumference height, weight and body mass index measurements. item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Tue Oct 27 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Tue Oct 27, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Intermediate Qualtrics — Tue Oct 27, 3:00 PM
item.description:
This course will cover topics beyond the scope of the Introductory to Qualtrics short course. We will take a deeper dive into Survey Flow features including embedded data, customizing the End of Survey experience, Screen Out Management, and implementing randomization. We will explore methods of importing embedded data into your survey, sending information from one survey to another, and setting embedded data in your survey through conditions within your survey. An introduction to automations will be illustrated through an example use case that sends respondents to a drawing survey after completing their survey. Finally, we will create custom reports to share with others in the ‘reports’ tab. Course material will be incorporated into a shared Group in which all participants will be added, offering hands-on practice with shared Libraries, and Directories. Additional features to be discussed include piping, authentication, and version management.

item.title: Pop The Cap | Anniversary Discussion and Toast — Thu Aug 13, 5:00 PM — Fullsteam ATC
item.description:
It's been 21 years since former North Carolina Governor Mike Easley signed HB 392 into law, raising the state's Alcohol by Volume (ABV) limit for beer from 6% to 15%. Fullsteam founder and owner Sean Lilly Wilson organized that movement, allowing brewers across the state to offer a much wider variety of products to beer drinkers. Come join him and others at Fullsteam's new ATC location for a panel discussion about the legacy of this legislation and all things beer in the Old North State, followed by beer and cake!
